International scholarships Get help with the cost of study. Find out more about our generous scholarships and how to apply for them. How it works Apply Apply to study a course at ARU. You do not usually need to apply for scholarships (but check individual scholarship pages for details). Review We review your application and check if you are eligible for any ARU scholarships. Confirm If you are eligible, we will offer you the highest value scholarship. You cannot usually combine scholarships. Discount You may also be able to get a Full Payment Discount of £1,000. Our scholarships International Undergraduate Scholarship International Postgraduate Scholarship Other ARU scholarships Full Payment Discount Save £1,000 in your first year of study, if you pay your tuition fees in full before teaching starts. See payment dates and deadlines . Other sources of funding UK Council for International Student Affairs The UK Council for International Student Affairs (UKCISA) has information about funding for international students looking to study in the UK. Postgrad Solutions study bursaries Postgrad Solutions offers 15 bursaries across a number of subject areas. Apply now . Global Study Awards The Global Study Awards encourage young people to study abroad, and explore new countries, cultures and languages. You can get up to £10,000 to expand your horizons. Maximum of nine awards available. Chevening Chevening is the UK Government’s international awards scheme aimed at developing global leaders. It offers Chevening Scholarships and Chevening Fellowships. Recipients are selected by British embassies and high commissions around the world. To apply, visit the Chevening website . Contact us Got a question? Speak to our international team. [email protected] Call +44 1245 683680 Complete our contact form Instagram

International scholarships International Undergraduate Scholarship Starting an undergraduate degree at ARU? This scholarship can help with the costs of study. The scholarship is a fee discount. We will deduct it from your tuition fees in each year of your course. Value There are two levels of award. Lower award – up to £5,000 £2,000 in the first year of your course* £1,000 in each subsequent year of your course (up to a maximum of three subsequent years) You must successfully complete each year to get £1,000 in the subsequent year *If you are studying at ARU in Writtle, you will automatically get £2,000 in your first year. Higher award – up to £7,000 £4,000 in the first year of your course £1,000 in each subsequent year of your course (up to a maximum of three subsequent years) You must successfully complete each year to get £1,000 in the subsequent year Eligibility You should be: an international student (international tuition fee payer) a new student, joining ARU for the first time starting a taught undergraduate course at ARU in Cambridge, Chelmsford, Peterborough or Writtle studying full-time, unless there are exceptional circumstances preventing full-time study starting in Year 1 to receive £2,000 (Lower Award) or £4,000 (Higher Award) If you are starting in Year 2 or Year 3, you will receive £1,000 in each year of your course. If you have Accredited Prior Certified Learning (APCL), discounts will be adjusted on a pro-rata basis. This scholarship cannot be combined with any other scholarships. However, you can get a Full Payment Discount in Year 1 if you pay your fees in full before teaching starts. The scholarship is not available during work placements or for: pre-sessional English courses ARU College courses foundation degrees online / distance learning courses degree apprenticeships or other work-based degrees Study Abroad programmes Depending on the terms and conditions of your funding body, you may not be eligible if you are: sponsored by an organisation such as an employer, charitable body, or government department receiving federal tuition fee loans How to apply There is no need to apply. You will automatically receive our International Undergraduate Scholarship if you meet the eligibility criteria. You must meet all conditions of registration before the scholarship is awarded. If you withdraw from your course, we will adjust the scholarship on a pro-rata basis. How we assess your application We review applications from all eligible international students. For the Lower Award, we assess the overall standard of your application, including entry qualifications. For the Higher Award, we assess the overall standard of your application. It should exceed minimum requirements, including entry qualifications. Questions? Speak to our international team. Email [email protected] or call+44 1245 683680. How to apply Step 4 - Receive our decision on your application We aim to provide an initial response and/or a decision on your application as soon as possible. Provided you meet our English, academic and immigration requirements, you'll be likely to receive an offer from us. Accepting your offer If you applied to us directly, you need to accept your offer on your Applicant Portal within 28 days (or sooner depending on when you applied). You will receive instructions on how to access your Portal in your offer letter. If you applied to us through UCAS, you will need to accept your offer through UCAS Hub . You will need your UCAS Personal ID and password to log in, which UCAS will have provided to you when you applied. Deadlines apply so please refer to the UCAS website to check for the deadline to accept your offer. Meeting your conditions To meet the requirements of a conditional offer, you’ll need to provide copies of all documents requested (for example, academic qualifications and English language test results. You can upload all your required documents to your Applicant Portal. Sometimes, we may come back to you and ask for additional supporting documents. This will be communicated to you via your Applicant Portal and by email. Therefore, it's very important that the contact details on your application form are correct and up to date and that you check your email regularly for correspondence from us. Paying your deposit Aside from any academic conditions, you will also be asked to pay a deposit. Please note that all full fee paying international students will be required to pay a deposit before being issued with a CAS . Currently, the deposit for Undergraduate and Postgraduate taught courses is £4,000; further details will be included in your offer letter. Refunds of any deposit paid will be administered in accordance with the Rules, Regulations and Procedures for Students, which you will receive with your offer letter. A refund of a deposit may not be given in the event of a refusal of a visa arising from giving false or incomplete information to the United Kingdom Visas and Immigration (UKVI). To pay your deposit, as well as your fees, visit our fee payments page . Issuing your CAS Before we issue a CAS, you'll need to complete our Immigration History Form. You may also be asked to provide us with the documents you are going to use for your visa application. For more information about obtaining a CAS, please visit our immigration page . Once you receive your CAS, you'll be able to apply for your visa, although keep in mind that it will be issued no earlier than three months before the start date of your course . I haven't heard from you yet... Check your email, including the junk folder. We may have requested further information or additional documents from you. Contact your country representative or agent (if applicable). If you're a direct applicant and you haven’t heard from us in ten business days, please email [email protected] .
